note: The almanac of Boon.land — wonders a reader can collect (book/scripts/modules/almanac.mjs). Canon: .spw/surfaces/almanac.spw. `terms` are matched in the prose, case-insensitively; `home` is where each is first met, `echoes` where it returns.

wonders.name: Torch-ants
wonders.note: Keep lit streets along the berry roots all winter, so the field never freezes through. Businesslike; very particular about torches.
wonders.hint: Something keeps the field warm from underneath.

prompt.vantage: cheek to the frost at the lip of a dug furrow, a working dog's nose an inch from an ant street cut open in the loam
prompt.light: frost-white grey dawn above; below, pinprick torches tallow-yellow and ember-warm along the berry roots, the only warmth in the field
prompt.scent: thawed loam, ant-smoke like a snuffed wick, cold berry juice, a bread-warmth under the frost
edges: a torch-ant relighting a neighbour's torch from the right corner while the whole street waits
a single-file detour of pinpricks bending around the break in their street
teal boonberries asleep under ice above the roots, each keeping an amber drop of light
a child's ear-print pressed into the rime at the top of the furrow
prompt.hint: cross-section of a frost-bitten berry field at grey dawn, tiny torch-ants keeping lamp-lit streets along loam-dark berry roots, single-file torch processions, one ant relighting a torch at the correct corner while the street waits, ice-sleeping teal berries above with amber cores, warm from underneath, painterly, businesslike wonder

wonders.name: Echo-wrens
wonders.note: Small brown wrens that sing a beat late. They nest in hollow cedars; a wren-call is the grove saying again.
wonders.hint: A bird in the grove that is always a little behind.

prompt.vantage: belly-low in old leaves at the grove's rim, looking up the split trunk of a hollow cedar where a wren pair nests
prompt.light: green noon strained through cedar canopy, teal in the shade, with brighter pollen-gold rings hanging in the air where a sound is about to come again
prompt.scent: shredded cedar bark, crushed fern, wet moss, resin on a woodcutter's axe
edges: three hollow cedars in a row, a small brown wren at each knothole, beaks opening one after another
a woodcutter's axe stopped mid-swing at the clearing edge, a chip still in the air
a shaggy dark working dog mid-sneeze, the cedars answering it one at a time
a faint second wren a beat behind each real one, like a print taken twice
prompt.hint: small brown wrens singing from the knotholes of hollow cedars, each a beat late after the last, faint after-images trailing their open beaks, a woodcutter's axe paused at the clearing edge, green noon through moss-thick grove, gold pollen rings in teal shade, painterly, wren-quick, gently comic

wonders.name: The lag-stag
wonders.note: A white stag nobody has seen. Its hoofprints press into the moss a beat after it has passed.
wonders.hint: Prints in the grove, with nothing to make them.

prompt.vantage: nose down in the moss at the grove's edge, a working dog's height, the freshest hoofprint filling the foreground
prompt.light: moth-soft evening under the trees, teal shade deepening, a low amber glow from the field behind; nothing anywhere to cast a shadow into the prints
prompt.scent: wet moss, crushed fern, cold air with no musk, no breath, no warm hide in it at all
edges: a line of cloven prints pressing into the moss one after another with nothing above them
the newest print still sinking, moss fronds springing outward around it
a low cedar bough swaying though there is no wind
a dark dog's muzzle in the nearest print, finding no scent
prompt.hint: moss-thick grove floor at dusk, a trail of large cloven hoofprints pressing into the moss one by one with nothing above them, the newest still sinking, a low bough swaying without wind, empty air where a white stag should be, teal shade, faint amber glow, painterly, hushed, unseen

wonders.name: Rehearsal moths
wonders.note: Dusk moths whose wings carry tomorrow’s weather, a little smudged. The grove keeps its almanac on them.
wonders.hint: Wings that know the weather early.

prompt.vantage: nose-level with the cedar bark as the moths come off it into the dusk
prompt.light: moth-soft evening under the trees; each wing faintly lit by the small weather painted on it
prompt.scent: old paper, cedar bark, cooling moss, rain that has not arrived yet
edges: one wing smudged with drizzle, another with a hard white glare like light off salt
the biggest moth carrying a grey-green storm sitting on a tiny hill
a moth slowly opening and closing its wings so the rain on them comes and goes
through a gap in the trunks, a far hill under the same grey-green storm the biggest moth carries
prompt.hint: dusk moths the colour of old paper coming off cedar bark, each wing smudged with tomorrow's weather, a drizzle on one, a white salt-glare on another, a grey-green storm over a tiny hill on the largest, wings opening and closing the rain, moth-soft grove light, painterly, intimate

wonders.name: Salt-whales
wonders.note: Vast, slow creatures under the salt flats. The flats are the roof of their road; their old roads glow under the crust.
wonders.hint: Something enormous moves under the flats.

prompt.vantage: nose an inch off the salt crust where the flats begin, one paw lifted and set down carefully, never stamping
prompt.light: last level amber raking the crust; every salt ridge throws a long teal shadow; beneath, gold whale-roads glowing up through the grains
prompt.scent: dry salt pan, hot dust cooling, cold brine rising through the cracks, a salt-raker's weathered rope
edges: two glowing whale-roads converging under the crust toward the same turn
the vast dim flank of a whale sliding beneath translucent salt like weather under ice
a salt-raker's wooden rake laid flat on the roof of the road
a ring of flat black signal stones small on the horizon
prompt.hint: endless cracked salt flats at amber dusk, glowing gold roads running beneath the translucent crust, a vast slow whale shape gliding under the salt like weather beneath ice, two roads bending toward one turn, salt-stiff ridges throwing teal shadows, low horizon, painterly, immense, patient

wonders.name: Signal-skinks
wonders.note: Finger-long lizards that bask on the signal stones and flick their tails in a code only the stones answer.
wonders.hint: Small tails, flicking a message on warm stones.

prompt.light: low amber sun on flat black stones; each stone answering a flick with a faint ember-warm pulse at its centre
prompt.scent: hot stone, dry salt, scorched sand, paint long since worn off
edges: a salt-pale skink mid-flick, its tail blurred like a pen stroke: short, short, long

prompt.hint: a ring of flat black signal stones on cracked salt flats at sunset, finger-long salt-pale skinks basking and flicking their tails busy as a clerk's pen, each stone answering with a faint ember-warm glow, a worn signpost at the centre, long teal shadows, painterly, curious, precise

wonders.name: The weathercocks
wonders.note: Iron roosters of Council Hill that vote by turning. The crosswind is their disagreement made weather.
wonders.hint: Iron that turns with an opinion.

prompt.light: split sky: warm gold sunbreak dawnward, cold teal squall rushing off the far ridge; rust-red combs catching the gold
prompt.scent: rain on one cheek and dry dust on the other, wet wool cloaks, cold iron, crushed gorse

wonders.name: Hum-crickets
wonders.note: Live in the Rift’s crack and keep its pitch. They go silent when someone lies near the floor.
wonders.hint: A small chorus that lives in a crack.

prompt.light: wide calm afternoon light through clean arched windows; one hairline of dark the light will not cross; a faint gold glow down inside the crack
prompt.scent: seed-cake crumbs, linseed floor wax, stone dust, cold tea gone glassy

wonders.name: Pane-snails
wonders.note: Glass-snails that graze soot off Bonk City’s panes at night. Their slow trails are how a pane is forgiven clear.
wonders.hint: Something cleans the city’s glass by night.

prompt.scent: chalk, cold rain, lamp soot, damp mortar
edges: silver snail-trails looping through the soot, each one a clear window onto a wet step, a cat on a sill, a corner

wonders.name: Gate-pigeons
wonders.note: Sleep on the parcel gate’s counterweight and ride it up and down all night without waking.
wonders.hint: Birds that sleep on something moving.

prompt.scent: pigeon-down, wet flour sacks, lantern smoke, cold iron

wonders.name: Oath-moths
wonders.note: Grey market moths drawn to sworn words. They settle in the oath groove only when a promise is true.
wonders.hint: Moths that can tell a true promise.

edges: lint-grey moths settling one by one along a groove of blueberry juice, wings shut flat as purses

wonders.name: Remembrancers

wonders.hint: A click in the timber, when something is too heavy.

wonders.name: Crown-wasps
wonders.note: Build paper crowns in the bloom garden, beautiful and hollow. A rented crown is wasp-work.
wonders.hint: Somebody builds crowns out of paper.

wonders.name: Early bees

wonders.name: Two springs, one bed
wonders.note: What the boatmen call the rivers: sharing one bed without forgetting where each came from. A membrane, not a merger.
wonders.hint: What the boatmen call the rivers.
wonders.craft: Separable layers (PLAN.E architecture): content and engine share one book without either whitening the other.

wonders.name: Leave room for the path
wonders.note: Pencilled in the margin of the archive's map: a record should leave a way through it. Every shelf keeps a gap.
wonders.hint: Something pencilled in a margin.
wonders.craft: Nothing is a dead end (c027): every wonder, card and chapter links onward; the last line stays open.

wonders.name: Keep the morning, not the week
terms: keep the morning, not the week
wonders.note: How a dog keeps time, and why Boof had the day nobody kept: attend to what is here, not to what the calendar says is.
wonders.hint: How a dog keeps time.
wonders.craft: Attend to the increment in front of you; the calendar is a projection, the morning is the work.

wonders.name: A box for what you do not know
terms: a box for what you do not know
wonders.note: What the records clerk says a good form needs after the night of the three records: one box left honestly open.
wonders.hint: What a good form needs.
wonders.craft: Types that admit the unclassified: a schema with room for what it cannot name yet is a schema that lasts.
